sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Groupe XXI (Chaga) sample = chaga-ouest (mashami, rwa, siha), chaga centre (wunjo, mochi), chaga-est, gweno; Kahe is not sampled (0 hits for kahe/E64). General statement that Chaga combines a fully distinctive tone system with an 'accent démarcatif' (p. 289, 366) applies to Vunjo/Mochi data, not Kahe.

sources.citation: Kahigi, Kulikoyela K. 2008. Kikahe: Msamiati wa Kikahe-Kiswahili-Kiingereza na Kiingereza-Kikahe-Kiswahili (Kahe-Swahili-English and English-Kahe-Swahili Lexicon). LOT Publications Lexicon Series 13. Dar es Salaam: Languages of Tanzania Project, University of Dar es Salaam. xv+105 pp. [publisher preview, 8 pp.: title, copyright, Introduction pp. iii-v, sample pp. 59-61]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Intro sec. 2 'Phonemes and Orthography' (pp. iii-v) covers consonants, NC clusters, five vowels ('difficult to state whether or not the language has a short-long vowel contrast'), nasal assimilation, post-nasal strengthening, gliding, pre-NC vowel lengthening; no tone, stress or accent section, and entries carry no tone/accent marks. p. iii: 'Kikahe is still completely undescribed (as far as I know!)'. Only pp. iii-v of the xv-page intro are in the preview; the intro's plan sentence announces only orthography/phonemes, entries and morphology.

sources.citation: Philippson, Gérard & Marie-Laure Montlahuc. 2003. Kilimanjaro Bantu (E60 and E74). In D. Nurse & G. Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, 475-500. London: Routledge.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kahe [Ka.] (E64) listed under Central Kilimanjaro (sec. 1.2); only Kahe-specific phonological remark is segmental ('/pf/.. apparently /p/ in Ka.'). Sec. 3 Tone characterises KB languages generally (tone shift, SH/H/L surface contrast; accent only mentioned via McHugh's analysis of Vunjo) and names M., Mo., W., S.R. (probably S., Rw., K.) as tonally attested, adding 'some of those are completely unknown tonally' -- Kahe is not among the attested ones. No stress/accent statement for Kahe.
